Accessibility

secure-code-agent is a command-line tool and a GitHub Action. Everything it produces is text: terminal output, a Markdown report, JSON, SARIF and a Markdown work order. This page says what that means for people using assistive technology, what is known not to work well, and how to report a barrier.

Commitment

Every finding, gate result and work-order item is available as plain text. No information exists only in a chart, a colour or an image: the Markdown report and the JSON carry the same findings, so a reader who cannot use one presentation can use the other.

Supported environments

  • Terminal output is plain text with no colour codes, so it reads the same in a screen reader, a braille display or a log file. Colour codes that a scanner prints are stripped before they reach the report.
  • The project site (the landing page and the example report) declares its language (lang="en") and loads no script or stylesheet from elsewhere; its data sits in HTML tables with header cells.
  • Language: reports are in English. The README has short machine-translated summaries in Spanish, German, French, Hindi and Simplified Chinese.

Known limitations

  • Reports are long. A full report lists every finding, including the test tree's, which are reported but not scored.
  • Markdown tables are wide. The scanner table and the findings tables have many columns, which read cell by cell in a screen reader.

Reporting a barrier

Open an issue at https://github.com/marshallguillory86/secure-code-agent/issues and say which output you were using (terminal, Markdown, JSON, SARIF or the site), the assistive technology involved if any, and what you could not do. Barriers are treated as defects.

Rendered from ACCESSIBILITY.md in the secure-code-agent repository. The markdown is the source of truth.
